steps: Welcome to the architect professional course: a year of defensible decisions at Meridian. In week one, the C F O hands you two point four million dollars and eight weeks, and your decision record with service level gates must clear the board.

In week nine, the pilot holds four hundred and eighty thousand documents. Access control filters by role at retrieval, before anything reaches Claude, using hybrid dense, keyword and structured search.
By week eleven, you are eight hundred and forty thousand dollars over budget. Prompt caching and routing between Haiku and Sonnet must cut forty percent, with service levels intact.
In week fifteen, the thirty-four tool claims agent drifts, so you decompose it into four subagents, turn on tool search, and put a human approval gate on payouts.
In week nineteen, the chief compliance officer demands proof before patient health data flows: Enterprise, a B A A and zero data retention, since Pro and Team offer no B A A. The board approves.
In week twenty-three, three incidents hit with no trace I Ds, and an A B test turns out p-hacked. So you rebuild observability and evaluations, remembering that parity is not fairness.
In week twenty-seven, the canary goes live at five percent of clinicians, on-call gets the runbooks, and any breach triggers an automatic rollback as it widens toward one hundred percent.
Finally, exam day: sixty-two questions in about ninety-five minutes, with single choice, select two, and scenario questions. A year at Meridian backs every answer.
